headline: Austan Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, has said price rises from the AI building boom are spreading beyond data-centre supplies and he fears they reflect overheating demand.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 1: the Semafor interview is dated 12 Oct, before the 13 Oct window; the facts match the headline, but the official also says he cannot split inflation between AI, oil and tariffs.
importance_line: Prices pushed up by AI spending reaching everyday goods would hit households first, then the Fed's choice on whether to raise interest rates again later this month, then the companies borrowing to build, but Goolsbee says he does not know the shares of AI, oil and tariffs, and that overheating is only "starting".
summary: Semafor reports, from an interview for its Compound Interest podcast, that Austan Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said price rises tied to the AI boom are "jumping out of its lane" and now reach beyond data-centre parts into unrelated parts of the economy, which he fears is "straight, old-fashioned overheating demand", and that if inflation stays persistent "it's clear what the Fed has to do". Semafor adds that prices of land, electricity, water, construction and electrical parts for data centres have surged but have not yet clearly reached items such as groceries, that US inflation was 3.4% in August with September's figures due this week, and that Goolsbee, who is not on the Fed's rate-setting committee, joins it in 2027.
notes: Read from fulltext. The Semafor article is dated 12 Oct 2026 in its address; the interview date is not stated.
